verses.english: Linked Discourses 24.18
1. Stream-Entry
A Realized One Neither Still Exists Nor No Longer Exists
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: “Kismiṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṁ upādāya, kiṁ abhinivissa evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjati:
verses.english: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what, does the view arise:

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”
“Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

verses.pali: “Rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṁ upādāya, rūpaṁ abhinivissa evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjati:
verses.english: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form, the view arises:

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti …pe….
verses.english: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’ …
What do you think, mendicants?
Is form permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.” …

verses.pali: vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya:
verses.english: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”
“No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yampidaṁ diṭṭhaṁ sutaṁ mutaṁ viññātaṁ pattaṁ pariyesitaṁ anuvicaritaṁ manasā tampi niccaṁ vā aniccaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “That which is seen, heard, thought, known, attained, sought, and explored by the mind: is that permanent or impermanent?”
“Impermanent, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vā taṁ sukhaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: “But if it’s impermanent, is it suffering or happiness?”
“Suffering, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yaṁ panāniccaṁ dukkhaṁ vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya evaṁ diṭṭhi uppajjeyya:
verses.english: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would the view arise:

verses.pali: ‘neva hoti, na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘A realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists after death’?”
“No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imesu ca ṭhānesu kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhasamudayepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhepissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāyapissa kaṅkhā pahīnā hoti—
verses.english: “When a noble disciple has given up doubt regarding these six grounds, and has given up doubt in suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the practice that leads to its cessation,

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyano”ti.
verses.english: they’re called a noble disciple who is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

verses.pali: so attā no ca me siyā;
Anantavā ca taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīranti,
Neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇāti.
